_comment: What each destination actually accepts, so 'which platform next' is a
lookup and not a guess. `channel` is the only field that decides how much
hosted_feed     you publish ONE url, the platform re-reads it forever.
This is the only channel that is automated end to end
and free. Set once, updates itself.
bulk_upload     you upload a CSV. Every location at once, but a human
clicks upload. Repeatable in minutes, not hours.
paid_api        a real API. Fully automatable, and it costs money.
These also SYNDICATE downstream, which is why one of
them replaces dozens of the manual_form rows below.
manual_form     a form, an account, and usually a CAPTCHA. The browser
runner exists for these. Lowest value per hour spent.
`service_area_ok` is whether a business with no street address can be
listed. `unknown` means nobody has checked, and unknown means SKIP -- the
same rule citations.py applies to requires_street. Check it by opening
the form, then set true or false and date it in `checked`.
Costs and policies move. Anything with checked:null has NOT been verified
by us and must be before it is relied on.

platforms.name: Apple Business Connect
platforms.reaches: Apple Maps, Siri, Spotlight
platforms.how: Business Connect -> Locations -> add multiple locations. Multi-location accounts can point at a feed instead of uploading each time.
platforms.note: Listed as supporting NEITHER hide-address NOR service areas. Worse for these sites than assumed — do not plan around it.
platforms.value_note: Somebody searching on this map taps Call. That is a lead, not a ranking signal — which makes these worth MORE than a directory profile, not less. The price of entry is a real address and a verification step.

platforms.tier_why: Apple Maps and Siri; per BrightLocal it supports neither hide-address nor service areas

platforms.name: Bing Places for Business
platforms.reaches: Bing Maps, Bing local pack, Copilot answers
platforms.how: Dashboard -> Manage locations -> Bulk upload -> Download template. Up to 10,000 locations in one file.
platforms.note: Service-area businesses ARE supported: a ServiceAreas array of towns (US is a supported market) plus HideAddress:true, which keeps the address off search results. BUT AddressLine1 is listed 'Is required? Yes' -- the model is a real address you hide, not no address at all. A blank street will not pass.
platforms.checked_against: Bing Places for Business API documentation (BingPlaces_API_Latest.pdf, 77pp)

api.how_to_get: Sign in to the sandbox at https://bptestwebsite.cloudapp.net/, then email partneronbp@microsoft.com to be issued a PUID and a CLIENT CERTIFICATE.
api.auth: client certificate, issued only to trusted partners; separate certs for sandbox and production
api.verdict: Not a route for six listings. Bing points at the API for operators managing thousands; onboarding is a partner process with a certificate, not a signup.
api.note: Updates are FULL replacements: a field left out of the payload is deleted from the listing.
